---
title: "for (i in 1:length(x)) runs even when x is empty"
ref: LEN-03
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: silencieux
extrait: '1:length(c())'
reponse: '1 0'
attendu: "nothing, the loop should not run"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
x <- c()
for (i in 1:length(x)) {
  print(i)
}
```
:::

## Why

`length(x)` is 0, and `1:0` is not an empty sequence: it is the vector `c(1, 0)`, counting down from 1 to 0. The loop therefore runs twice, with indices that do not exist in `x`.

## The remedy

`seq_along()` and `seq_len()` return an empty sequence when they should.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
for (i in seq_along(x)) {
  print(i)
}
seq_len(0)
```
:::
